title: Three Ways Out
subtitle: The 8:15, the Holloway Rush and the Last Train over the Kill

setting.name: The Edges of Merriwick: Pier Point, the West Side and the Steeps
setting.description: Sunday and Monday — Days 4 and 5 of the Arrival. The scenario ranges the whole length of the island, because now the party knows the rule and the ways across the water are the only question left. At dawn on Sunday the Visitors lift the Sutter Street Bridge — the last road bridge, jammed solid with Thursday's traffic all week — in front of half the East Side. At 8:15 on Sunday three hundred people who heard the same radio broadcast the party did rush the Margaret Duane at Pier Point. On the West Side, Lt. Dana Castellane holds the Holloway Tunnel's ventilation building with three officers and four hundred people and has four blocks of plastic explosive and a plan for the tunnel jam. And at the very top of the island, past Harlow and the cliffs of the Steeps, the Northern Line's last diesel sits in the Kill Street yard beside a 1907 swing bridge that has stood open over Devil's Kill since 4:12 on Thursday. Every route works, once, if it is done In Pattern. Every route costs something. And every time survivors use one, the Visitors notice it, and close it.
setting.atmosphere: The scenario of hope and its price. For the first time the party is acting rather than surviving, and the players should feel clever and capable — and then watch how fast a crowd can undo cleverness. Sunday morning at Pier Point is the worst thing in the campaign: three hundred people Lifted off a ferry deck in a column of light, and three hundred pairs of shoes left behind in rows. The West Side is a military camp of frightened civilians under a commander who believes in force. The Steeps are wild — cliffs, woods, old forts, apartment blocks on granite — and the Ushers den there. The Visitors are no longer only patient: they are finishing something, and the clocks all over the island are converging on 4:12.

keyLocations.name: Pier Point and the Margaret Duane
keyLocations.description: The southern tip of the island: a waterfront park, an old round stone fort, the Harbor Acoustic Monitoring station, and the Pier Point Ferry Terminal — a 1950s glass-and-steel hall with three slips. The Margaret Duane, a 310-foot orange ferry, comes and goes on her timetable with her Set crew aboard: Captain Rosalind Akers at the wheel, mate Danny Ocampo at the ramp, deckhands Fitz and Little Joe. A mile out in Lower Bay stands the Harbor Lantern, taller than the Hallam Tower.
features: The terminal's waiting hall, departure board blank white, turnstiles still clicking
Slip 2, where the Margaret Duane docks every thirty minutes from 6:00 A.M. to 11:30 P.M., ramps down, ramps up, and goes
The rocks below the fort, where Walt Kubiak has been watching the boat for three days
The Harbor Lantern, a mile out: Dread DC 15 if anyone goes onto the water, and its Hush (Attention never falls below 2 on the Point)
encounters: Boarding the Margaret Duane to look at her
secrets: The Margaret Duane's Set crew run the full timetable perfectly; the boat crosses the Hem and docks at Calder Point and comes back — but only passengers who are In Pattern stay aboard across the Hem

The last scheduled departure before the 4:12 'gap' on a weekday is the 3:45. Walt calls it 'the light boat': it always ran nearly empty, because nobody leaves the city at 3:45. On Thursday, it will be the last boat ever

keyLocations.name: The Holloway Ventilation Building
keyLocations.description: A ten-storey brick-and-limestone tower on the West Side waterfront that houses the fans for the Holloway Tunnel, with a fenced yard, a garage of Tunnel Authority emergency trucks, and the tunnel plaza beside it. Lt. Castellane's shelter: four hundred people on cots on the fan-room floors, an aid station, a kitchen, three ESU officers and a truck.
features: The fan rooms: enormous, silent since the power failed, the best shelter on the West Side
The Tunnel Authority garage: three heavy tow trucks with amber lightbars, the kind that pull broken-down cars out of the tunnel every day
Castellane's command post: a map of the tunnel, a satellite phone, and a crate with four blocks of plastic explosive in it
A view across the Westwater to the mainland cliffs and the town of Halloran, lit every night, a mile and a half away
encounters: The Monday morning rush through the tunnel
secrets: The Tunnel Authority's own tow crews pulled stalled cars out of the Holloway every single day — amber lights, slow, by the book — which means towing in the tunnel, done right, is In Pattern
Castellane's brother Paul is in the 4:20 rows in the Greensward, and she has not gone to look

keyLocations.name: The Holloway Tunnel
keyLocations.description: Two tubes, each 1.6 miles long, under the Westwater: the inbound (to Merriwick) and the outbound (to Halloran on the mainland). At 4:12 Thursday the outbound tube was full of rush-hour traffic leaving the city, and it stopped. Most of the drivers got out and walked back toward the island — in the dark, shouting — and are in the Greensward now. Most of the cars are still there, bumper to bumper, a mile and six-tenths of them. The Hem crosses the tube about three-quarters of a mile in, under mid-river, as a faint shimmer in the air between two tiles.
features: The outbound tube: two lanes, tiled walls, a raised catwalk on one side, about 1,100 stopped cars, many with doors open
The inbound tube: clear — traffic into the city had thinned out by 4:12 — and the obvious route for anyone driving into Merriwick in the morning
Cross-passages between the tubes every 750 ft, with fire doors
The Glitter: a slow drift of it all along the ceiling by Sunday, thickening every hour; it fills the tubes solid by dawn on Tuesday, or sooner
encounters: A Stilt at the Halloran portal, if the Attention reaches 6
secrets: Traffic going INTO Merriwick on a Monday morning is the heaviest pattern in the tunnel's day: a bus that drives out through the outbound tube can drive back in through the inbound tube between 7 and 9 A.M. and be In Pattern, which means the convoy can make more than one trip
Each successful crossing teaches the Visitors. After the Monday rush, the Glitter fills both tubes by nightfall instead of Tuesday dawn

keyLocations.name: Harlow and Gansevoort Middle School
keyLocations.description: Harlow: brownstones, churches, wide avenues and a fierce, proud neighbourhood that has organised itself better than any other on the island. Gansevoort Middle School on 138th Street has been a shelter since Thursday, run by its principal, Dr. Celestine Abara, with two hundred children and staff. Hector's mother's walk-up is three blocks away on 141st.
features: Gansevoort Middle School: two hundred children, forty staff, a gym full of cots, and a principal who has kept every child quiet for four days
Desmond Pruitt, twelve, Lo's grandson, who has been helping in the kitchen and has not cried once in front of anybody
141st Street: Graciela Salgado, seventy-four, on the fifth floor with a bad hip and a canary, who has been feeding the whole building out of her pantry
The churches of Harlow, whose bells have been ringing the hours all week, slightly out of time with each other — and by Monday, in time
encounters: Moving two hundred children (the hardest Group in the campaign)
secrets: A school day is the strongest pattern for children on the island. Two hundred children walking in a crocodile, two by two, holding hands, with teachers at front and back, at 8:00 A.M. or 3:00 P.M., is so In Pattern that the Stilts step aside for it
Graciela Salgado will not leave without her canary, and a canary is very novel indeed in a train carriage

keyLocations.name: The Steeps and the Devil's Kill Swing Bridge
keyLocations.description: The north of the island: granite cliffs over the Westwater, old forts, Fort Tryon-like gardens, steep stairs between apartment blocks on the rock, and the last woods on Merriwick. At the very top, Devil's Kill: a hundred yards of fast tidal creek between the island and the mainland. The Northern Line crosses it on a two-track steel swing bridge built in 1907, which pivots on a central pier to let barges through. It was open at 4:12 Thursday. It is open now. The Kill Street rail yard and station sit at the island end, with a four-car Northern Line diesel train in the yard.
features: The swing bridge: 300 tons of steel on a pivot pier, open, its tracks pointing up and down the creek
The bridge-tender's house on the island bank: a brick hut with the swing motor (dead since Day 2), a manual capstan for emergencies (slow and loud), and the schedule board
The Kill Street yard: a diesel locomotive and four commuter cars, fuelled; a station platform; the schedule, still posted
The Ushers' den in the woods of the Steeps above the yard: a dozen of them, more than anywhere else on the island
encounters: Getting to the yard through the Steeps (Ushers)
secrets: The bridge was closed by its motor every night at 11:20 for the late trains, and opened at 1:00 A.M. for the barges. Closing it at 11:20, by the motor, is In Pattern. Closing it any other way is not
Every Northern Line train crosses the Hem in pattern if it runs on the timetable at line speed — and the 6:10 A.M. inbound comes back, if someone wants to bring it back

synopsis: Days 4 and 5. Armed with the rule and the radio report, the party goes to the edges of the island to find a way off — and finds three. At dawn on Sunday the Visitors lift the last road bridge in front of the East Side. At 8:15 three hundred people rush the Margaret Duane at Pier Point and the Harbor Lantern lifts them off her deck in a column of light, leaving three hundred pairs of shoes in rows; on the rocks below the fort the party meets Walt Kubiak, her engineer, who knows why. The ferry works for people who board it like commuters, and it cannot take a crowd. On the West Side, Lt. Dana Castellane wants to blow the Holloway Tunnel's jam with plastic explosive; the party can show her a better way — tow the jam the way the Tunnel Authority does it every day, and drive four hundred people out under the river in a Monday morning bus convoy, In Pattern. And at the top of the island, through Harlow and the Usher-haunted Steeps, the Northern Line's last train can cross Devil's Kill at 11:40 on Monday night if someone can close a 300-ton swing bridge the way it was closed every night, and if the party can bring two hundred schoolchildren and an old woman with a canary. Every route works once. Every route the survivors use, the Visitors close. By Monday midnight the party has saved hundreds, has learned what the Visitors are doing, and knows that what is left — the hospital, the Library, the Sleepwalkers, the Choir, and themselves — must go on the Last Ferry.
hook: Sunday, 6:40 A.M., the Library roof. Across the East Side, over the low roofs of Eastgate, the Sutter Street Bridge — the last road bridge, jammed solid with Thursday's traffic all week — rises out of the Tidewater with a sound like a long exhaled breath, turns once in the dawn, and drifts north toward the Greensward. On the crank radio, the mainland station is repeating the story of the eleven who walked off the ferry, over and over. And down on Bramwell Avenue, for the first time since Thursday, people are running — not from anything, but toward something: south, toward Pier Point, toward the 8:15. Dozens of them. Then hundreds. Peg Odinga watches them go and says, very quietly, 'Oh, no. Oh, no, no, no.'

acts.title: Act 1: The 8:15
acts.description: Sunday morning at Pier Point. The party arrives (in pattern, on foot or by Benny's bus) to find the terminal full of three hundred desperate people. The Margaret Duane docks at 8:00 and leaves at 8:15. What happens next is the campaign's worst moment, and the party may only be able to watch it. Then Walt Kubiak.
objectives: Reach Pier Point by 8:15 (or not — the party may arrive to the aftermath)
Try to stop, calm, or split the crowd, and learn what cannot be done
Meet Walt Kubiak, and learn the ferry's rules and the timetable
Go aboard the Margaret Duane and see the shoes
encounters: The crowd at the terminal (skill challenge; it cannot be fully won)
The Harbor Lantern turning (not a combat)

scenes.name: Three Hundred
scenes.description: The terminal's waiting hall is packed with people who heard the broadcast and ran here. They are pushing at the turnstiles. At 8:00 the Margaret Duane comes in from Calder Point, empty except for her Set crew, ramps down at Slip 2. At 8:15 she will sail, and three hundred frightened people are going to be on her.
scenes.readAloud: “The waiting hall of the Pier Point terminal is meant for a commute. It is not meant for this. Three hundred people, maybe more, pressed against the turnstiles and the glass, children on shoulders, suitcases, a man with a parrot in a cage, a woman in a wedding dress for some reason nobody will ever know. They are not quiet. They are the opposite of quiet. Out beyond the slip the Margaret Duane comes in out of the morning haze exactly on time, big and orange and absolutely ordinary, and through her wheelhouse windows you can see the captain at the wheel, calm, a cup of coffee by her hand, doing her job. Out beyond the boat, a mile out on the grey water, the Harbor Lantern stands taller than any building you have ever seen, lit from the inside like a paper lamp. It is perfectly still. It is, you realise, facing this way.”

skillChecks.skill: Intimidation or Persuasion (with a PA, a bullhorn, or Benny's headset)
skillChecks.success: You split the crowd: a few dozen listen and stay back — the ones with children, mostly. They will be at the Last Ferry on Thursday, and they will remember who told them to wait.
skillChecks.failure: They do not hear you, or they hear you and do not believe you. Nobody who has decided to get on a boat can be talked off it by a stranger in the time you have.

skillChecks.success: You see that this cannot be stopped, only shrunk, and you put your effort where it matters: the families nearest you.
skillChecks.failure: You keep trying to save everybody.

skillChecks.success: When the light comes, you are not in the crowd. You are standing on the terminal steps, still and quiet, and it passes over you.
skillChecks.failure: You were in the crowd when it began. Make a DEX save DC 13 to get clear before the light reaches the slip, or be Lifted with them — see dmTips about Lifted PCs.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This is a tragedy that the party cannot prevent, only reduce. Say so in the scene's texture, not out loud: let them try, let some of it work. The point is not to punish them for having heard the broadcast — it is to show them that the rule works only for people who can hold it, and that a crowd cannot.

scenes.name: The Column of Light
scenes.description: At 8:15 the Margaret Duane sails, three hundred people on her decks, crying and singing and shouting. She makes about six minutes out, almost to the Hem, and then the Harbor Lantern turns — the whole of it, slowly — and a column of soft light reaches across a mile of water to the boat, and lifts everyone off her decks. Up. In a long glittering stream into the Lantern. And the boat sails on, on her timetable, across the Hem to Calder Point, with her Set crew aboard, and nobody else.
scenes.readAloud: “For six minutes it looks like it is going to work. The boat goes out into the haze, low in the water, her decks black with people, and you can hear them from the shore: cheering, some of them, actually cheering. Then the Lantern turns. You have never seen it move and you would not have believed something that big could move without sound, but it turns, the whole of it, like a lighthouse beam finding a ship, and the light comes across the water to the boat. It is not bright. It is soft. And the people on the deck go up into it. All of them. Not falling, not struggling — rising, in a long slow glittering stream, like sparks going up a chimney, up and across a mile of air and into the Lantern, and the cheering stops, and there is no sound at all. The Margaret Duane sails on into the haze, on time.”

skillChecks.success: You watch it. All of it. Somebody has to.
skillChecks.failure: Shaken. You will not forget this either.

scenes.roleplayNotes: Hold the silence afterwards. Nobody died — the three hundred will be in the Greensward by noon, Set, filed in a new row — but the players will not feel that yet. On the rocks below the fort, an old man in a Carhartt jacket is standing with a flare pistol in one hand and an air horn in the other, and he has just used both. That is Walt Kubiak, and he thinks it was his fault.

scenes.name: Walt on the Rocks
scenes.description: Walt Kubiak has been watching the boat for three days. He knows her timetable to the minute, he knows her crew are Set and running her, and he has worked out, by watching, what the eleven Sleepwalkers did right on Friday: they boarded as commuters, sat in the cabin with their papers, and did not look out of the window. He blew the horn as the Lantern turned. He thinks that caused it.
scenes.readAloud: “He is sitting on the rocks below the old fort with an empty flare pistol across his knees and an air horn beside him, and he does not look up when you come down. He is a big, square, white-haired man in a Carhartt jacket with Harbor Ferries on the pocket, and there are orange ear defenders round his neck. ‘She’ll be back at nine,’ he says. ‘Eight fifty-two at the slip, ramp at eight fifty-four. She’s never late. Twenty-six years. Never late.’ Then he puts his face in his hands. ‘I blew the horn,’ he says. ‘I saw it turn and I blew the horn. Unscheduled signal. I did that.’”

skillChecks.success: He did not cause it. A crowd like that was at Attention 6 the moment it boarded; the Lantern was already turning. You can see that he will not believe it from you, today.
skillChecks.failure: Maybe he did. You do not know.

skillChecks.success: He talks. The timetable, the crew, the eleven, the 'light boat' at 3:45 that nobody ever rode. And the thing he has worked out that nobody else has: 'She crosses. She docks. Ramps go down at Calder Point and come up again. Whatever's on her that's in its seat with its paper, it stays on her and it gets off. You want to get people off this rock? Thirty at a time. Fifty. Commuters. Not that.' He nods at the water. He will join the party.
skillChecks.failure: He tells you to leave him alone. He will be on the rocks at 8:52, and at 9:22, and every half hour, and the party can come back.

scenes.roleplayNotes: Walt is the key to the Last Ferry and becomes a companion here. He is gruff, decent, practical and drowning in guilt. Do not have the party convince him of his innocence in this scenario — that is a thread for lf-scenario-004. Do have him give them the timetable, and the idea of the 3:45.
loot: The Pier Point–Calder Point weekday timetable, folded into eighths

scenes.name: The Shoes
scenes.description: At 8:52 the Margaret Duane comes back, on time, empty except for her crew. If the party goes aboard (walking on as passengers would, In Pattern, DC 10), they find her decks covered with shoes: three hundred pairs and more, sneakers and heels and work boots and a baby's red sandals, standing neatly in rows exactly where their owners stood. The wedding dress woman's satin shoes. The parrot, in its cage, alive, furious, the only living passenger.
scenes.readAloud: “The shoes are in rows. That is what you will remember. Not scattered, not kicked off — standing, toes forward, in exactly the places their owners were standing when the light took them, in neat ragged rows along the rail of the main deck from bow to stern. Work boots. A pair of child’s light-up sneakers, still faintly blinking. Two satin heels, white. In the wheelhouse above, Captain Rosalind Akers lifts her coffee cup, and sips, and puts it down, and lifts it again, and the boat rocks gently against the slip, and somewhere on the upper deck a parrot in a cage is screaming every swear word it knows.”

skillChecks.success: In the main cabin, five people are still sitting on the benches — alive, un-Set, rigid with terror, clutching newspapers they picked up from the rack. They did what the eleven did. They were not taken. They did not get off at Calder Point because they did not dare move. They are the proof.
skillChecks.failure: Shoes, and the Set crew.

skillChecks.success: Walt shows you her engine: fuelled for a week, running perfectly, her Set engineer's hands doing the right things on the controls. She will run until Thursday.
skillChecks.failure: A ferry. Running.

scenes.roleplayNotes: The five survivors in the cabin are the scenario's turn from despair to hope. They are why the party will trust the ferry on Thursday. Ask the players whether they want to ride the boat across with the five now. If a player character does, they are off the island and out of the campaign — make that clear. Most will not. If a PC wants to cross and come back to prove it, the boat comes back, and so do they: the return trip is In Pattern too.
loot: The parrot, if anyone wants it (it is very, very novel)

acts.title: Act 2: The Holloway
acts.description: Sunday afternoon to Monday 9 A.M. on the West Side. Lt. Dana Castellane, her shelter of four hundred, her explosives, and the argument. Then — if the party wins it — the Monday morning rush: tow the jam the way the Tunnel Authority does it every day, and drive a convoy of buses out under the Westwater, In Pattern.
objectives: Reach the Holloway ventilation building and meet Castellane
Talk her out of the explosives — with a demonstration, not a speech
Clear a lane in the outbound tube overnight, by the book
Run the Monday morning convoy between 7 and 9 A.M., and get as many people out as possible
encounters: The convoy (skill challenge; possibly a Stilt at the far portal)

scenes.name: Truck 3
scenes.description: The ventilation building is fenced, lit by a generator, and guarded by Officers Bianchi, Oyelaran and Dutra of ESU Truck 3 with carbines. Castellane meets the party in the fan room she uses as a command post. She has a map of the tunnel, a satellite phone and a crate of plastic explosive, and she has decided that at 0600 Monday she will blow a gap through the jam at the Merriwick end of the outbound tube and drive her people out. She has never seen a Lifting up close.
scenes.readAloud: “The fan room is the size of a church and as quiet as one, the great fans still and dusty, their blades taller than a man. Cots in rows. A child asleep with a teddy bear on a fan housing. At a folding table under a work light, a tall woman in an ESU tactical vest is bent over a map of the tunnel with a pencil, and she does not look up until she has finished the line she is drawing. ‘Lieutenant Castellane,’ she says. ‘ESU. I’m told you came from Pier Point this morning.’ She looks at your faces and something in her own changes very slightly. ‘Okay,’ she says. ‘Tell me.’ On the floor beside the table there is an olive-drab crate, open, with four grey blocks of something inside it, and wires.”

skillChecks.success: You argue her out of the explosives with words alone. This is very hard; she has a plan and four hundred people and she is a person who acts.
skillChecks.failure: She listens, politely, and says: 'Show me.'

skillChecks.success: She does not trust argument. She trusts evidence, demonstrated. If you show her the rule — not tell her — she will change her mind completely.
skillChecks.failure: She seems immovable.

scenes.roleplayNotes: Castellane is not a villain. She is the best person on the island in any other disaster. Run her as respectful, exhausted, sharp. She calls the party by their surnames. She will not be talked out of her plan; she will be shown out of it. If the party fights her and her officers, they are fighting three trained shooters with carbines in a building full of civilians, and it will be the worst decision of the campaign.

scenes.name: Show Me
scenes.description: The demonstration. The party has to prove the In Pattern rule to Castellane in front of her own eyes: walk past a Stilt on the West Side Highway at a commuter's pace; play a Lullaby next to a Glitter swarm and then make a noise; drive Benny's bus down the highway at 30 mph past an Usher pair. And they can show her the opposite: what a single gunshot does. She may also insist on testing her own way: shooting a Stilt.
scenes.readAloud: “‘All right,’ Castellane says. She has her carbine slung, and she is standing very still at the fence of the ventilation yard, watching the Stilt that has been walking the West Side Highway since Thursday step carefully between the abandoned cars, two hundred yards north, reading a fire hydrant. ‘All right. You walk out there. You walk past that. If it doesn’t take you, I’ll listen.’ Behind her, Officer Bianchi says, ‘Lieutenant —’ and she says, ‘I know,’ without turning round.”

skillChecks.success: You walk down the West Side Highway past the Stilt at the pace of a man going to buy a paper, and it reads a hydrant beside you and does not look up, and you walk back. Castellane watches the whole way through binoculars. When you come back through the gate she says, 'Okay,' very quietly, and puts the explosives crate under her own cot. She is now on your side, completely.
skillChecks.failure: You flinch at fifty feet. The Stilt turns. Make another check at DC 17 or be Lifted — and if you are Lifted, Castellane will open fire to get you back, which is a disaster.

skillChecks.success: June or Haddad stages the Lullaby demonstration on the Glitter at the tunnel portal: the swarm ignores a dropped wrench beside the speaker, then drifts straight to the same noise when the speaker is off. Advantage on the Persuasion check to stand down the explosives.
skillChecks.failure: The Glitter does something unclear. Castellane is unconvinced.

skillChecks.success: After any successful demonstration, she agrees: no explosives. She asks what you would do instead, and when you tell her about the tow trucks, she smiles for the first time.
skillChecks.failure: She agrees to wait one day. She keeps the crate.

enemies: 1 Stilt (only if Castellane opens fire, or the party tries to kill it)
combatEncounters.difficulty: Deadly for the district, survivable for the party
combatEncounters.tactics: If Castellane and her team fire on the Stilt (she has the carbine at +4 for 2d6+2; her officers are SWAT Officers), it Hums and Lifts whoever is nearest and Out of Pattern. If they bring it below 20 HP it folds and sounds the falling tone: the Attention on the whole West Side goes to 6 and the adjacent districts to 4; four Ushers arrive in 1d4 rounds and a second Stilt in 1d6; and the Harbor Lantern turns toward the West Side for an hour. The ventilation building's four hundred are now in danger and must stay absolutely silent until dawn. This is what killing one costs, and if Castellane does it, she sees it, and she never fires on a Visitor again.
combatEncounters.terrain: The West Side Highway: eight lanes of abandoned cars (engine blocks are full cover), the tunnel plaza, the ventilation yard fence, the Westwater bulkhead.
combatEncounters.statblock: STILT (Large aberration, CR 4). AC 15 (lacquered carapace). HP 68 (8d10+24). Speed 30 ft, climb 20 ft. STR 18 (+4) DEX 12 (+1) CON 16 (+3) INT 14 (+2) WIS 16 (+3) CHA 5 (-3). Saves WIS +5. Skills Perception +7. Resistances piercing, bludgeoning. Vulnerabilities thunder. Condition immunities frightened, charmed. Senses tremorsense 120 ft, blindsight 30 ft; it does not see light at all. Pattern-Blind: it cannot perceive a creature that is In Pattern unless the scene's Attention is 6 or that creature has harmed it. Dread: WIS save DC 12 on first sight (campaign rules). No Anatomy: called shots and Precision Strike-style bonus damage from 'vital spots' do not apply; criticals still double dice. Actions — Multiattack: two Lift attempts, or one Hum. Lift: melee +6 to hit, reach 10 ft, one creature: 2d6+4 bludgeoning (it is not trying to hurt you; that is just what its grip does) and the target is grappled (escape DC 15). On its next turn it carries a grappled creature toward the nearest Lantern at full speed; a creature carried out of sight is gone, and returns Set within the hour. Hum (recharge 5-6): a 30-ft cone of resonance; CON save DC 13, 3d8 thunder damage and Shaken on a failure, half damage and not Shaken on a success. Glass in the cone breaks (+1 Attention). Behaviour: a Stilt walks streets slowly, bending to 'read' anything novel with a fan of fine glassy filaments; it Lifts whatever is Out of Pattern and ignores everything else. It does not pursue into buildings narrower than its 10-ft frame, does not go underground, and if reduced below 20 HP it stops, folds, and gives a long falling tone that sets the Attention in the whole district to 6. Killing one is possible. It is almost always a mistake. ESU officers: use LookupMonster 'SWAT Officer'.

scenes.roleplayNotes: Let this be the players' best moment of being right. Castellane's turn is total: once she believes, she is the most effective ally on the island, and the ESU officers become the convoy's marshals. If she does fire on the Stilt (because the party could not prove it, or because a PC was Lifted), let the dice decide, and let the consequence fall on the West Side.
loot: The ESU's radios (channel 4), first-aid kits, and the use of the truck

scenes.name: Tow Crew
scenes.description: Overnight Sunday to Monday, someone has to clear one lane of the outbound tube — a mile and six-tenths of stopped cars — by 7 A.M. The Tunnel Authority's three tow trucks are in the garage. Towing in the tunnel, done exactly as the Authority's crews did it every day (amber lightbars on, slow, one car at a time, hazard lights on the tow, no horns, no shouting), is In Pattern. Done any other way it is noisy work in a tiled tube that carries sound for a mile, under a ceiling of Glitter.
scenes.readAloud: “The amber lights turn the tube into a long yellow throat. Tile, tile, tile, the curve of the ceiling, and above the cars a slow drift of something glittering along the roof of the tunnel like dust in a projector’s beam, thicker the further in you go. The tow truck’s engine is loud in here. It is meant to be. Walt — or whoever is at the wheel — says, very quietly, ‘By the book. Lights on. Slow. One at a time. Like it’s a Tuesday and somebody broke down.’ The first car is a silver hatchback with a child seat in the back and a cardboard coffee cup on the dash. Eleven hundred to go.”

skillChecks.success: You run the tow by the book. Each success clears a quarter of the lane (four successes needed, one per two hours of work). Characters can rotate; a Tech's Jury-Rig gives advantage on one check.
skillChecks.failure: A tow cable snaps, a car alarm goes, a door slams. +2 Attention in the tube; the Glitter comes down off the ceiling onto the tow crew (Static) unless they freeze, and that quarter takes another two hours.

skillChecks.success: The tow truck moves like a tow truck moves on a Tuesday. Advantage on the next Mechanics check.
skillChecks.failure: You clip a car. It is loud. +1 Attention.

skillChecks.success: Three-quarters of a mile in, you see the Hem: a faint shimmer in the air between two tiles, across the whole tube. The cars on the far side of it are the same. The Glitter is thickest here. Somebody has written on the tile, at head height, in silver paint, 'KALLA'. She has been here, on Thursday night, alone, as far as the last tile before the shimmer — and then she turned round.
skillChecks.failure: Tile, cars, light.

enemies: 2 Glitter swarms (if the Attention in the tube reaches 2 or more)
combatEncounters.tactics: The swarms drift down onto whatever is making noise and use Static on anyone who strikes them or shouts. Fire disperses them (and is +1 Attention); a fire extinguisher deals them 2d6 cold; freezing and waiting in a running tow truck's cab for a round makes them drift back up. Every round of fighting is +1 Attention, and at 4 a Stilt walks to the Merriwick portal and stands in it, reading, until dawn.
combatEncounters.terrain: A tiled tube, two lanes of stopped cars, a raised catwalk, cross-passage fire doors every 750 ft, amber light.
combatEncounters.statblock: GLITTER (Medium swarm of Tiny aberrations, CR 1). AC 12. HP 22 (5d8). Speed 0 ft, fly 30 ft (hover). STR 3 (-4) DEX 15 (+2) CON 10 (+0) INT 1 (-5) WIS 12 (+1) CHA 1 (-5). Resistances bludgeoning, piercing, slashing. Immunities grappled, paralyzed, prone, restrained, frightened. Senses blindsight 60 ft. Swarm: it can occupy another creature's space and move through openings an inch wide; it cannot regain HP. Record: the Glitter remembers every sound made within 30 ft of it. It replays them later, elsewhere, at random — a dead man's voice, the party's names, a gunshot — and each replay in a scene is +1 Attention. Harmless in Pattern: a Glitter swarm does not attack anything unless it is struck, sprayed, burned or shouted at from inside it. Actions — Static: every creature in the swarm's space makes a CON save DC 12, 2d6 lightning damage on a failure, half on a success (1d6 if the swarm is at half HP or less). Behaviour: drifts like dust in a sunbeam, towards novelty. It is the Visitors' ears. Fire disperses it (a burning swarm takes double damage), and a fire extinguisher's cone deals it 2d6 cold.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This is a long, slow, tense night of honest work, and it is a good place for the party to talk — about who goes and who stays, about the Set, about Thursday. Let it be quiet. If Calla is with the party, her tag on the tile beside the Hem tells the players that she walked a mile under the river alone on Thursday night to see whether the Hem was real, reached the shimmer, painted her name, and lost her nerve — and that she has never told anyone. She will talk about it if asked gently.

scenes.name: The Monday Rush
scenes.description: Monday, 7:00 to 9:00 A.M.: the heaviest traffic in the Holloway's day. The convoy — Benny's bus #14 and as many West Side Transit Authority buses as the party can find drivers for (Castellane's officers, Benny, Walt, Lo, any civilian with a licence) — drives out through the cleared outbound lane at 30 mph, in lane, headlights on, past the Hem, to Halloran, and then drives back in through the inbound tube at commuting speed for another load. Each bus carries up to 60 people as a Group; each must hold Calm through a mile and six-tenths of Glitter and the shimmer of the Hem.
scenes.readAloud: “Four buses in a line at the mouth of the tunnel at seven in the morning, engines running, headlights on, sixty people in each one sitting in their seats with their hands in their laps and their eyes on the backs of the seats in front, because that is what you do on a bus. Benny is at the wheel of the first one, and he has his headset on, and he is talking — not loudly, steadily, the way he has talked to a busload of strangers ten thousand times: ‘Good morning, everybody, and welcome to the Holloway Tunnel, opened in nineteen twenty-seven, one point six miles, the first mechanically ventilated underwater vehicular tunnel in the world…’ The bus rolls forward into the yellow light. Behind you on the plaza, Castellane raises one hand. Above the tunnel mouth, the Glitter shifts on the ceiling like something turning over in its sleep.”

skillChecks.success: The bus holds its lane and its speed for a mile and six-tenths.
skillChecks.failure: The driver brakes, swerves or sounds the horn. +2 Attention in the tube; that bus's Group must make its Calm check at disadvantage.

skillChecks.skill: Keep Walking (each bus Group, led by whoever is aboard)
skillChecks.success: Through the Hem. A shimmer passes down the length of the bus like a sheet of water, and nobody moves, and then you are through, and the far portal is grey daylight, and Halloran, and the National Guard. The Group is out.
skillChecks.failure: Someone in the bus screams at the shimmer, or stands up, or tries to get off. The bus is Out of Pattern at the Hem. It slows. It turns, gently, in a tube too narrow for a bus to turn in, and drives itself back to the Merriwick portal, and everyone aboard who was not In Pattern is Set. Benny's Rally (or any reroll feature) can be used once per bus.

skillChecks.success: A driver who reaches Halloran persuades the National Guard checkpoint (which is very confused) to let them turn around and drive back in through the inbound tube for another load. Each round trip takes about 40 minutes; there is time for two or three.
skillChecks.failure: The Guard will not let the bus go back. That driver is off the island.

enemies: 1 Stilt at the Merriwick portal (if the tube's Attention reaches 4)
combatEncounters.tactics: It stands in the portal reading each bus as it goes in. Any bus that is In Pattern passes beneath it. Any bus Out of Pattern is stopped and its passengers Lifted. Do not fight it; drive under it.
combatEncounters.statblock: STILT (Large aberration, CR 4). AC 15 (lacquered carapace). HP 68 (8d10+24). Speed 30 ft, climb 20 ft. STR 18 (+4) DEX 12 (+1) CON 16 (+3) INT 14 (+2) WIS 16 (+3) CHA 5 (-3). Saves WIS +5. Skills Perception +7. Resistances piercing, bludgeoning. Vulnerabilities thunder. Condition immunities frightened, charmed. Senses tremorsense 120 ft, blindsight 30 ft; it does not see light at all. Pattern-Blind: it cannot perceive a creature that is In Pattern unless the scene's Attention is 6 or that creature has harmed it. Dread: WIS save DC 12 on first sight (campaign rules). No Anatomy: called shots and Precision Strike-style bonus damage from 'vital spots' do not apply; criticals still double dice. Actions — Multiattack: two Lift attempts, or one Hum. Lift: melee +6 to hit, reach 10 ft, one creature: 2d6+4 bludgeoning (it is not trying to hurt you; that is just what its grip does) and the target is grappled (escape DC 15). On its next turn it carries a grappled creature toward the nearest Lantern at full speed; a creature carried out of sight is gone, and returns Set within the hour. Hum (recharge 5-6): a 30-ft cone of resonance; CON save DC 13, 3d8 thunder damage and Shaken on a failure, half damage and not Shaken on a success. Glass in the cone breaks (+1 Attention). Behaviour: a Stilt walks streets slowly, bending to 'read' anything novel with a fan of fine glassy filaments; it Lifts whatever is Out of Pattern and ignores everything else. It does not pursue into buildings narrower than its 10-ft frame, does not go underground, and if reduced below 20 HP it stops, folds, and gives a long falling tone that sets the Attention in the whole district to 6. Killing one is possible. It is almost always a mistake.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This is the scenario's triumph. Let it be a real one: four hundred people out, maybe seven hundred, under the river, in buses, because the party worked out the rule and an old tour guide talked the whole way. Track the number. Then, at dusk on Monday, the Glitter fills both tubes solid — a day early, because they noticed — and the Holloway is closed. The players should feel both things.
loot: Castellane's gratitude, and her sat phone's attention

acts.title: Act 3: The Last Train over the Kill
acts.description: Monday. The party (or part of it) goes north through Harlow to the Steeps: Lo's grandson and two hundred children at Gansevoort Middle School, Hector's mother on 141st Street, Calla's brother Nico in the Steeps. The Northern Line's 11:40 from Kill Street can cross Devil's Kill on Monday night if the swing bridge is closed the way it was closed every night — and if the party can get the children to the yard through the Ushers' woods.
objectives: Reach Harlow and the Steeps in pattern (a Monday commute, the school run)
Collect Desmond Pruitt, Graciela Salgado, Nico Moreno, and the children of Gansevoort
Get the swing bridge closed at 11:20 by its motor (generator, Jury-Rig) — or some other way, at a cost
Run the 11:40 across the Kill, In Pattern, at line speed
encounters: The crocodile: two hundred children through the Steeps (skill challenge)
The Ushers' woods (Hard for level 3; evasion preferred)

scenes.name: Harlow
scenes.description: Harlow has organised itself: block captains, church kitchens, a bell-ringing schedule. Gansevoort Middle School is a shelter of two hundred children under Dr. Celestine Abara, fifty-five, who has kept every one of them quiet for four days with a rigid timetable. Desmond Pruitt, twelve, Lo's grandson, is on kitchen duty. Graciela Salgado, Hector's mother, is three blocks away on the fifth floor with a canary called Tito.
scenes.readAloud: “The school gym is full of cots and children and absolute order. A timetable written on a whiteboard — Breakfast 7:30, Lessons 8:30, Quiet Reading 10:00 — and two hundred children sitting at their cots reading, actually reading, in silence, while a tall woman in a grey suit walks the rows with her hands behind her back. In the doorway to the school kitchen, a skinny twelve-year-old in an apron too big for him looks up from a tray of sandwiches, sees who is standing in the gym doorway, and drops the tray.”

skillChecks.success: Dr. Abara agrees to bring her two hundred to the Kill Street yard tonight — as a school trip: a crocodile, two by two, holding hands, teachers at the front and back, at a walking pace, singing nothing. She runs it like a fire drill.
skillChecks.failure: She will not move them at night. She will move them at 3:00 P.M., at school dismissal time, which is In Pattern but means hours waiting at the yard, in the Steeps, near the den.

skillChecks.success: Graciela comes, with Tito in a cage under a towel. Covered, the canary is quiet.
skillChecks.failure: Graciela will not leave without Tito, uncovered, singing. A singing canary is +1 Attention every hour.

scenes.roleplayNotes: Give the reunions their time. Lo and Desmond, Hector and Graciela, Calla and Nico (whom she finds at her aunt's, in the Steeps, an hour later). These are the moments the players have been carrying for four days.
loot: Two hundred children, forty staff, Desmond, Graciela, Tito (keep the tally)

scenes.name: The Crocodile
scenes.description: Moving two hundred children and forty adults two miles north from Harlow through the Steeps to the Kill Street yard. A school crocodile is the strongest pattern a child has, and it works — until a child cries. The route passes the edge of the Ushers' woods.
scenes.readAloud: “Two by two. Holding hands. Teachers at the front and the back and every twenty yards in between, and Dr. Abara at the very front in her grey suit with a clipboard, setting a pace that would not hurry a funeral. Two hundred children, walking up the long hill of Steeps Avenue in the late light, absolutely silent. In the woods above the road, something moves. Something low and glassy, keeping pace in the trees. Then another. A seven-year-old near the back looks up at the trees and her lip starts to go.”

skillChecks.success: The crocodile holds. The Ushers in the trees pace it, and lose interest, and fall back.
skillChecks.failure: A child cries. The Group loses 1 Calm and +1 Attention. Somebody needs to get to that child and make it stop — Rally, Persuasion DC 12, or Hector picking her up and carrying her like a sack of rice while making her laugh (Performance DC 13).

skillChecks.success: Someone — Benny, a teacher, a child — starts a quiet counting game, the kind of thing a school does on a trip. It is In Pattern. Advantage on the crocodile's next check.
skillChecks.failure: The game is louder than you meant.

skillChecks.success: Teo's Trailwise takes the crocodile down the stairs on the cliffside instead of along the woods' edge: steeper, slower, safer.
skillChecks.failure: You stay on the road along the woods.

combatEncounters.difficulty: Hard (for a level 3 party protecting children)
combatEncounters.tactics: If a child runs, the Ushers come out of the trees for the child and try to Herd her into the woods. They Nip only those who interfere. The party's job is to stop the child running and hold everyone still — an Usher that feels no movement for a round loses track. Gunfire here is +3 Attention and a catastrophe: the whole crocodile will break.
combatEncounters.terrain: A steep avenue along the edge of the woods, a stone retaining wall (full cover), cliff stairs with iron rails, parked cars.
combatEncounters.statblock: USHER (Medium aberration, CR 2). AC 14 (folded glass plates). HP 33 (6d8+6). Speed 50 ft. STR 14 (+2) DEX 18 (+4) CON 12 (+1) INT 6 (-2) WIS 14 (+2) CHA 3 (-4). Skills Perception +4, Stealth +6. Resistances piercing. Senses tremorsense 60 ft. Pattern-Blind (as Stilt). Herding: it has advantage on attack rolls and shoves against any creature that moved more than 10 ft on its last turn — running is the thing it hunts. Stillness: an Usher that cannot perceive movement in a creature for a full round (the creature took no move and no action except Keep Walking or Dodge) loses track of it and circles. Actions — Nip: melee +6 to hit, 1d8+4 piercing. Herd: the Usher shoves a creature up to 10 ft in a direction of its choice (contest: its Athletics +2 with advantage from Herding if applicable, against the target's Athletics or Acrobatics); used to push people toward a Stilt or a Lantern. Bonus action — Chime: it rings like a struck glass; every Usher within 300 ft knows where it is (+1 Attention). Behaviour: Ushers come in twos and fours and work like sheepdogs, not wolves. They want to drive runners toward a Stilt to be Lifted. They bite only what resists. They break off when nothing in the scene is moving fast.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This is the protect-the-civilians test the campaign has been building to, before the Last Ferry. Two hundred children are the hardest Group in the game. Let it be terrifying and let it mostly work.

scenes.name: The Bridge-Tender's House
scenes.description: The swing bridge has been open since 4:12 Thursday. It closed every night at 11:20 by its electric motor for the late trains. The motor has been dead since the power failed on Day 2. Options: (a) Jury-Rig a generator to the motor and close it at 11:20 exactly — In Pattern, Mechanics DC 15, 10 minutes' prep; (b) the manual capstan — four people, twenty-five minutes of grinding steel, +1 Attention every five minutes in the den's earshot; (c) something worse.
scenes.readAloud: “The bridge-tender’s house is a brick hut on the bank with a single window, a desk, a kettle, a calendar from a marine-supply company and a big, old, green-painted electric motor connected to a gearbox the size of a car. On the wall by the door there is a board in a glass case: SWING SCHEDULE. CLOSE 23:20. OPEN 01:00. In the dark beyond the window the bridge stands open across the creek, three hundred tons of black steel on its pivot pier with its tracks pointing at nothing. Across the water, a hundred yards away, the mainland is lit. You can hear a dog barking over there. You can hear a car.”

skillChecks.success: Walt (or the party's Tech, with Jury-Rig and a generator from the yard) wires the generator to the motor. At 11:20 exactly the motor turns over with a sound it has made every night for a hundred years, and the bridge swings closed. In Pattern.
skillChecks.failure: The motor will not take it. You have twenty minutes and a capstan.

skillChecks.success: Four people at the capstan bars, walking in a circle in the dark, for twenty-five minutes. The bridge comes round. The Attention has risen by 5.
skillChecks.failure: The pawl slips. It comes back two feet with a bang. +2 Attention, and five more minutes.

skillChecks.success: June or Haddad realises the timing matters as much as the method: the bridge must finish closing as close to 11:20 as possible. Close it too early and it is novel for longer.
skillChecks.failure: You close it when you can.

enemies: 1 Stilt and 1d4+2 Ushers (if the Attention at the yard reaches 6)
combatEncounters.tactics: The Ushers come out of the woods for anything moving; the Stilt walks down onto the yard tracks and reads the train. If the train is Out of Pattern when it moves, the Stilt Lifts from it. Anyone who stays at the capstan or the motor is Out of Pattern when the train passes. The only answers are to get everyone aboard and still, run the train on time, and leave someone behind — or not.
combatEncounters.terrain: The rail yard (ballast, rails, a platform), the bridge-tender's house, the bridge itself (100 yards of steel deck, no rail on the outer edge), the creek below (fast, cold, and the Hem down the middle of it).
combatEncounters.statblock: STILT (Large aberration, CR 4). AC 15 (lacquered carapace). HP 68 (8d10+24). Speed 30 ft, climb 20 ft. STR 18 (+4) DEX 12 (+1) CON 16 (+3) INT 14 (+2) WIS 16 (+3) CHA 5 (-3). Saves WIS +5. Skills Perception +7. Resistances piercing, bludgeoning. Vulnerabilities thunder. Condition immunities frightened, charmed. Senses tremorsense 120 ft, blindsight 30 ft; it does not see light at all. Pattern-Blind: it cannot perceive a creature that is In Pattern unless the scene's Attention is 6 or that creature has harmed it. Dread: WIS save DC 12 on first sight (campaign rules). No Anatomy: called shots and Precision Strike-style bonus damage from 'vital spots' do not apply; criticals still double dice. Actions — Multiattack: two Lift attempts, or one Hum. Lift: melee +6 to hit, reach 10 ft, one creature: 2d6+4 bludgeoning (it is not trying to hurt you; that is just what its grip does) and the target is grappled (escape DC 15). On its next turn it carries a grappled creature toward the nearest Lantern at full speed; a creature carried out of sight is gone, and returns Set within the hour. STR 14 (+2) DEX 18 (+4) CON 12 (+1) INT 6 (-2) WIS 14 (+2) CHA 3 (-4). Skills Perception +4, Stealth +6. Resistances piercing. Senses tremorsense 60 ft. Pattern-Blind (as Stilt). Herding: it has advantage on attack rolls and shoves against any creature that moved more than 10 ft on its last turn — running is the thing it hunts. Actions — Nip: melee +6 to hit, 1d8+4 piercing. Herd: the Usher shoves a creature up to 10 ft in a direction of its choice (contest: its Athletics +2 with advantage from Herding if applicable, against the target's Athletics or Acrobatics); used to push people toward a Stilt or a Lantern. Bonus action — Chime: it rings like a struck glass; every Usher within 300 ft knows where it is (+1 Attention). Behaviour: Ushers come in twos and fours and work like sheepdogs, not wolves. They want to drive runners toward a Stilt to be Lifted. They bite only what resists. They break off when nothing in the scene is moving fast.

scenes.roleplayNotes: The bridge is the cost of this route made physical: whoever closes it by hand is in the tender's house when the train goes, a hundred yards from its doors. Making it to the train is an Athletics DC 18 sprint along the platform onto a moving car — Out of Pattern, at the Hem. A PC or NPC who stays can walk home along the Kill in pattern at dawn, and will be alive on Thursday for the Last Ferry. Make the players say who stays. If Walt is here he will volunteer, and his reason will be the horn.

scenes.name: The 11:40
scenes.description: The four-car Northern Line diesel leaves Kill Street at 11:40, crosses the bridge at line speed, passes the Hem at mid-creek and runs on to the mainland's first station, Spuyten Landing, at 11:46. Each car is a Group. The driver must run it like the 11:40 has always been run — Lo has ridden this line on duty; Walt can drive anything with an engine; Benny drove for the Transit Authority. Piloting DC 14.
scenes.readAloud: “The cab lights come on. The horn — two short, the departure — and the train moves, slowly at first, out of the yard and onto the bridge, steel on steel, the sound of every late train you have ever heard going home. In the four cars behind you, two hundred children and forty adults and an old woman with a towel over a birdcage sit with their hands in their laps. The bridge deck is under you. Below, the black water of the Kill. Ahead, halfway across, a faint shimmer in the air across the whole width of the track, like heat over a road. You are doing exactly the right speed. Forty yards. Twenty. Somebody in the second car whispers, ‘Mommy,’ and a teacher’s hand goes over her mouth, and the shimmer passes down the length of the train like a sheet of cold water.”

skillChecks.success: Line speed, no horn but the scheduled one, no braking. The train is In Pattern.
skillChecks.failure: The train jerks or slows at the Hem. Every car's Group checks at disadvantage.

skillChecks.success: Through. Spuyten Landing, the lights of the mainland, a confused stationmaster and then a great deal of noise from very happy people.
skillChecks.failure: That car is Out of Pattern at the Hem. The train goes on; that car's passengers are lifted out through its windows in a long soft stream, and are in the Greensward by morning. The car arrives empty.

scenes.roleplayNotes: The scenario's second triumph, and probably its most dangerous moment. Track the tally. At midnight on Wednesday the Northern Line closes (a Stilt swings the bridge open again and stands on it), but after a run like this the Visitors notice and close it at dawn Tuesday instead. If the driver wants to come back on the 6:10 A.M. inbound, they can — it is In Pattern. The party reaches level 4 at the end of this act. Then Haddad, back in the city, puts the last piece together (see twists).
loot: Up to two hundred and forty saved (keep the tally)

npcsInvolved.name: Walt Kubiak, 58
npcsInvolved.role: Companion NPC / the Margaret Duane's engineer
npcsInvolved.description: Has watched the boat from the rocks for three days and knows her timetable, crew and rules. Joins the party in Act 1. See his companion file.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Get people off on the boat, the right way; wake his crew; atone for the horn.

npcsInvolved.name: Lt. Dana Castellane, 41
npcsInvolved.description: Holds the Holloway ventilation building with three officers and four hundred people; has plastic explosive and a plan; changes her mind on demonstrated evidence. See her companion file.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Get her four hundred off by any route; keep her officers alive; do her duty — which is about to become a problem.

npcsInvolved.name: Officers Bianchi, Oyelaran and Dutra
npcsInvolved.description: Three tired, decent, well-armed police officers loyal to Castellane. Use SWAT Officer statblocks. If she is convinced, so are they; they become the convoy's marshals.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Their lieutenant, and the people in the fan room.

npcsInvolved.name: Captain Rosalind Akers and the crew of the Margaret Duane
npcsInvolved.description: Captain Akers (fifty, at the wheel, lifting her coffee), mate Danny Ocampo (at the ramp), deckhands Fitz and Little Joe, and engineer Oskar Brandt below. They run the timetable perfectly.
npcsInvolved.motivation: None that they know. Walt talks to Akers every time he goes aboard.

npcsInvolved.name: Dr. Celestine Abara, 55
npcsInvolved.description: Has kept two hundred children quiet and safe for four days with a timetable and absolute authority. Runs the crocodile like a fire drill.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Every child. She will be the last off the train.

npcsInvolved.name: Desmond Pruitt, 12
npcsInvolved.description: Skinny, serious, has been on kitchen duty for four days and has not cried in front of anybody. Will cry in front of his grandmother.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To be useful. He wants to stay with Lo, wherever she goes, and that includes back into the city.

npcsInvolved.name: Graciela Salgado, 74
npcsInvolved.description: Fifth-floor walk-up on 141st, bad hip, a canary called Tito, has been feeding her whole building from her pantry. Thinks the Visitors are 'very rude' and says so.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Tito. And her son, who she will scold for not coming sooner.

npcsInvolved.name: Nico Moreno, 8
npcsInvolved.description: At their aunt Yesenia's in the Steeps. Small, quiet, worships Calla, has drawn the Stilts in crayon two hundred times.

npcsInvolved.name: The Five
npcsInvolved.role: Survivors in the Margaret Duane's cabin
npcsInvolved.description: Five people who boarded the 8:15 and sat in the cabin with newspapers and were not taken: a hotel night porter, two nursing students, a retired schoolteacher and a sixteen-year-old boy. They are the proof the ferry works.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To get off this boat. If asked, they will ride her across and back to show the party.

rewards.money: Nothing that matters. Castellane's shelter has a generator, fuel, food and medical supplies, and she will share all of it with a party that has saved her people.
items: The Pier Point–Calder Point weekday timetable (from Walt)
Castellane's satellite phone's attention (if she trusts the party), and the ESU's radios on channel 4
A Tunnel Authority tow truck, a West Side Transit bus or two, and Benny's bus #14 if it came back
Castellane's four blocks of plastic explosive, if she gives them up (she will not, until Thursday)
The tally of people saved by the Holloway rush and the 11:40, which should be several hundred
rewards.story: The party ends Monday night having used two of the three ways out, and having watched the Visitors close each one behind them. Whoever is still on the island — the hospital, the Library, the Sleepwalkers, the Choir, anyone who stayed at the bridge, and the party themselves — must go on the Margaret Duane, and the last boat is the 3:45 on Thursday. The xp figure is per character: it takes each from level 3 to level 4.

twists: THE CROWD IS THE DANGER. The ferry works. It worked for the eleven and the five. It cannot take three hundred panicking people. The tragedy of the 8:15 is not that the rule failed but that it cannot be followed by a crowd.
TOWING IS IN PATTERN. The Tunnel Authority cleared breakdowns from the Holloway every day; the jam can be cleared by doing exactly what they did. The party's best solution is the most boring one.

EVERY ROUTE USED IS A ROUTE CLOSED. The Visitors notice. The Holloway fills with Glitter at dusk on Monday instead of dawn Tuesday; the Kill bridge is swung open and held by a Stilt at dawn Tuesday instead of midnight Wednesday. The party will realise they are teaching the Visitors where the edges are.

WHAT THEY ARE DOING (Haddad, Monday night). The clocks all over the island now agree with each other to the second. The Set are filed by time. The Visitors recorded the city and played it back to check it. The rows, the bridges laid down whole, the Hem, the routes closing from the largest to the smallest: they are finishing a copy. Haddad says it out loud for the first time: 'They are not taking us. They are keeping us. They are keeping the island. Like a recording. Like a specimen. And when it is finished — Thursday, 4:12, one week to the second — whatever is inside the frame is in it forever.'

WEXLEY. If the party passes the Hallam Tower on the way north, they learn that on Saturday the billionaire Anton Wexley took off from his helipad on the roof with his family and his security in a private helicopter. The helicopter came back. It is sitting on the helipad. Everyone in it is Set, seatbelts on, looking out of the windows at a view of the mainland that is always just about to arrive.
dmTips: THREE ROUTES, ONE PARTY. The party may want to do everything; they cannot be at the Holloway at 7 A.M. Monday and Harlow by 3 P.M. without moving fast, and the 11:40 is that night. Let them split, and use the ESU radios to cut between groups. If they choose only one route, the other closes unused — and its people (Gansevoort's children, or Castellane's four hundred) must come down the island on Thursday to the Last Ferry, which makes lf-scenario-004 much harder. That is a fine outcome.
THE 8:15 IS NOT THE PARTY'S FAULT. Make that clear in play, by having Walt — who blames himself — be so obviously wrong about it that the players see the same thing in their own guilt.

LIFTED PCs. By this scenario a PC who is Lifted and not rescued in two rounds is Set in the Greensward. They can be woken by an ally (CHA (Persuasion) DC 15, advantage for close bonds), which costs a day's travel and an Attention spike at the Great Lawn. Keep it a real cost, not a death. The player plays an NPC companion until then.

CASTELLANE'S EXPLOSIVES. If she blows the jam anyway (because the party could not convince her), the explosion is +4 Attention, the Harbor Lantern turns toward the West Side, the Glitter fills the outbound tube from the Hem outward within an hour, and nobody gets through. Her four hundred are now Last Ferry passengers. She will be devastated, and from that moment she follows the party's lead without question.

TRACK THE TALLY. By the end of this scenario the party should know a number — 'four hundred and twelve through the Holloway, two hundred and thirty-one on the 11:40' — and so should you. The epilogue of lf-scenario-004 is built from it.

PCs LEAVING. A PC who rides a bus or the train out is off the island; a PC who drives back in on the inbound rush or the 6:10 is not. Make each crossing a choice, and honour a player who decides their character's story ends on the far shore.
LEVEL UP. The party reaches level 4 after the 11:40.
